Jonathan — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the friction. A couple quick notes and immediate next steps: 

- What likely happened: our calendar generator embeds an encoded join token in the Meet URL; some mail clients (and corporate gateway scanners) URL-encode/modify that blob and the token becomes invalid on arrival.
- Short-term fix: we can reissue a plain (non-embedded-token) Meet invite or spin up a temporary Zoom room and send the new join info now.
- Ownership/permissions: if Indigo wants to delegate moderator rights (so your admin can admit people), we can include a moderator link and/or mark Ben or Priyom as alternate hosts.

I’ll prepare a regenerated invite and a Zoom fallback. Ben / Priyom — can you confirm availability to claim host/alternate-host on the Zoom room if we go that route?

Attaching proposed agenda and the original .ics so we can compare.

Rishi

Hi Rishi,

We looked up the meeting id you referenced (internal ref 842-xx-xx). Our logs show 3 failed join attempts between 11:00 and 11:05 UTC for user agents that stripped query parameter punctuation during URL normalization. This is a known edge case with some mail gateways. Workarounds: 1) use a short redirect (redwood.io/j/842) in the calendar body, or 2) set alternate hosts via account settings and share the static Zoom join URL (no embedded token).

If you want us to temporarily whitelist IndigoTech’s mail gateway for a single meeting, we can do that if you provide the gateway IPs.
